cards.explanation: The answer is that he has walked with integrity. David says, "For I have walked with integrity; I have trusted in the LORD without wavering." He doesn't hand over a trophy list. He points to how he has walked. Plain and steady, friends, and I respect that.

The answer is True. David says, "I have trusted in the LORD without wavering." Without wavering means he kept leaning on the LORD, not just on the easy days. I wobble when I carry a full tray of hot cookies across the kitchen, so that kind of steady is impressive to me.

The answer is False. David says, "Test me, O LORD, and try me; examine my heart and mind." He doesn't leave his heart off the table. He asks the LORD to examine his heart and mind. I think that takes nerve, friends.

The answer is the LORD's loving devotion. David says, "For Your loving devotion is before my eyes, and I have walked in Your truth." What's before his eyes is the LORD's loving devotion. And in the same breath, he says he has walked in the LORD's truth.

The answer is deceitful men. David says, "I do not sit with deceitful men, nor keep company with hypocrites." Deceitful men come first, and hypocrites follow right behind them. Those are the two kinds of company he names.

The answer is hates. David says, "I hate the mob of evildoers, and refuse to sit with the wicked." It's a strong word, and he puts it in the song plainly. His seat choice matches it: he refuses to sit with the wicked.

The answer is so he can go about the LORD's altar. David says, "I wash my hands in innocence that I may go about Your altar, O LORD…" The washing is for going about the LORD's altar. He's getting ready to be in the LORD's presence, friends.

The answer is False. David says he'll go about the altar "…to raise my voice in thanksgiving and declare all Your wonderful works." Thanksgiving is what he plans to raise his voice for. He also plans to declare the LORD's wonderful works.

The answer is the house where the LORD dwells. David says, "O LORD, I love the house where You dwell, the place where Your glory resides." I'll tell you, my bakery feels like home to me, but David is talking about something even bigger, bakers.

The answer is that David asks the LORD not to take his soul away with sinners. He says, "Do not take my soul away with sinners, or my life with men of bloodshed…" Then he describes those men: wicked schemes in their hands, and bribes in their right hands. That's the company he doesn't want to be taken away with.

The answer is True. David says of them, "…in whose hands are wicked schemes, whose right hands are full of bribes." Wicked schemes are in their hands. Their right hands carry bribes too. Compare that to David washing his own hands in verse 6, friends.

The answer is that he asks the LORD to redeem him and be merciful. David says, "But I will walk with integrity; redeem me and be merciful to me." He ends his promise with a request for mercy. I think that's a humble way to follow up a strong claim.

The answer is bless. David closes with, "My feet stand on level ground; in the congregations I will bless the LORD." The song opens with David asking to be vindicated and ends with him blessing the LORD. He plans to do it in the congregations, with other people around.
